name: aidc-dev
comment: This devcontainer.json supports VS Code's Dev Containers extension as a SECONDARY entry point.
Primary entry point is `aidc create <name>` which uses compose + the full proxy/policy/audit stack.
What VS Code path gives you:
- The same image as aidc create (Python 3.12/3.13/3.14 + pyenv + uv + poetry + pipenv,
Go, Rust, Node, Claude Code, docker-in-docker, native wheel build deps, psql)
- VS Code's IDE features (extensions, terminals, language servers)
What VS Code path does NOT give you:
- The Squid blocklist proxy
- The policy sidecar / taint detection
- The audit aggregator
- Bridged Claude Code auth, settings, memory, and ~/.claude.json
- The git-identity bridge from your host config
- `aidc-claude --continue` auto-resume
Features (DinD, common-utils, git) are deliberately omitted. They are already baked into
the Dockerfile, and the upstream DinD feature has historically lagged new Ubuntu LTS
releases (it did not support 24.04 at the time; unverified against 26.04) — so leaving
it in would risk breaking the VS Code build for no benefit.
DinD nuance: VS Code overrides our ENTRYPOINT with its own keep-alive loop, so the
entrypoint script (which normally starts dockerd) never runs. postStartCommand below
calls the standalone aidc-dockerd-start.sh as root to spin up dockerd every time the
container starts. It is idempotent — re-running while dockerd is already up is a no-op.
